walkthrough: Goal: practise V大's combined lines (two to four lines in one frame, joined, crossing, branching or near one another) the way I copy single lines, and start every session after the first with a short warm-up of what I already know, then move on to the stage's newer exercises; a session stays about 20 to 30 minutes.

First session (as before, shorter): Today, Start practice. Six single lines, then four groups of combined lines, then six colours. I copy the first line and compare it, skip on to the first colour, match it and compare, and go on to Finish. The summary counts lines, combined lines and colours apart. One more.

Warm-up: the second session opens on 'Warm-up 1 of 4': two single lines and two colours, kinds I compared before, about five minutes; no instructions pop up (I know these), How still has them. I copy the warm-up line, compare, and go on: the warm-up's colours have the inline wheel as any colour does.

The mix: after the warm-up the bar reads 'Line 1 of 6', then after six lines 'Combined lines 1 of 4'. The first time combined lines come up their instructions show by themselves: see the whole group as one shape first, its outer ends and corners and where lines meet or cross; fix those key points lightly with Sketch; then the inside, each line between its points, in sure strokes with Draw, never erasing; compare, don't guess.
Copy: I mark the group's key points with Sketch (never judged), then draw each line with Draw, a little off as a hand is.

Compare: the whole original group lies over my lines in the thick semi-transparent red, in place (where it lies in its frame), so my placement shows. One tap on Aligned: the group moves and sizes onto my lines as one shape (never turned; my sketch marks left out), so only the shape's errors show. The pen has turned blue: I correct the worst line in blue over the old one; the red goes as my pen lands. Compare again: the red comes back over the corrected copy, aligned as I chose.
Chinese: All tools, Actions, 中文: the bar reads '组合线条 1/4', How brings the 组合线条 instructions in Chinese, the compare card says 对齐 and 原位; the warm-up reads 热身. Back to the exercise's own tools.
Summary: Finish shows the whole sheet with the warm-up's pairs first; the card counts lines, combined lines and colours compared, and the colours' radar and means beside my first session.
Not here: numbers for lines (the overlay is the feedback); combined lines of my own choosing; other stages' warm-up kinds.
